name: Trust-First Peter
summary: Peter is not a viable acquisition target for a paid Visa product. He might accept a completely free card as a rare backup but will never make it primary. Marketing spend on this segment should focus on trust-building and ATM accessibility, not product features.

price_sensitivity.finding: Avoids all fixed costs by default. Picks the free card even when variable fees would likely cost more. Peace of mind trumps financial optimization.
price_sensitivity.key_quote: Paying CHF 8 every month does not feel justified to me.

feature_preference.finding: No feature convinces him. Even forced to choose, foreign fee waiver is 'maybe' — but he rarely travels. Cashback distrusted, welcome bonus dismissed as confusing.
feature_preference.key_quote: None of these really convince me.

behavior_switching.finding: Does not use Twint — cash and PostFinance are the baseline. Would need full understanding and proven safety before even considering any change. Extremely resistant.
behavior_switching.key_quote: I would need to fully understand how it works and be sure it is safe.

trade_off.finding: Rejects net gain on principle — monthly calculations create anxiety, not confidence. Prefers the certainty of cash over any mathematical advantage a card might offer.
trade_off.key_quote: I prefer not to depend on such calculations every month.

willingness_to_pay.finding: CHF 5 is the absolute ceiling, only if the product is simple, safe, and free of hidden conditions. Would maybe take a free card as a rare backup — but would not use it daily.
willingness_to_pay.key_quote: At most CHF 5, and only if it is very simple and clearly safe.

visa_recommendation.viable_product: Free Visa card as emergency backup only — no paid product viable
avoid: any product requiring calculations or tracking
visa_recommendation.acquisition_trigger: Trust and safety messaging only — not features or savings
visa_recommendation.segment_note: Low ROI segment for acquisition. More relevant for retention and ATM network messaging.
